newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel expects to cut loss in half in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel expects to cut loss in half in 1997.

text.p: Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel expects to cut its losses by more than half this year, its chairman said Thursday, as shareholders prepared to vote on a plan to restructure its massive debt load.
Executive Chairman Patrick Ponsolle said Eurotunnel will post a net loss of $456.2 million in 1997, compared with a loss of $1.0 billion in 1996.
Ponsolle told an extraordinary meeting of the company's shareholders, held for a vote on a debt restructuring plan, that the net loss would fall by "more than 50 percent."
Holders of 920 million Eurotunnel shares were to vote on a 70 billion franc ($11.7 billion) debt restructuring deal reached by Eurotunnel and its banks in April.

The improvement in the results would stem from lower interest charges of $543 million, compared with $957 million in interest paid in 1996, assuming the debt restructuring plan were approved, he said.
Eurotunnel's operating income was forecast to rise 73 percent, to $86.3 million, Ponsolle said.

The French and British governments last week agreed to extend Eurotunnel's license by 34 years to at least 99 years -- provided the debt plan is accepted and rail freight traffic increased through the tunnel -- in return for 25 percent of its net profits from 2052.
